ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Proceeds of Crime (Act No. 6517, as amended), the Korean Commercial Act (Articles 19, 19-2, 289 and related provisions), Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 17410, as amended), financial company supervisory regulations issued by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), and FATF Recommendations 10, 22, 24 and 25 as implemented in the Republic of Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of foreign parent/promoter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent/promoter corporate registry in its jurisdiction of incorporation; for a domestic promoter, the relevant Korean district court commercial registry.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in origin -> if origin is an Apostille Convention state, obtain apostille from the designated Competent Authority (Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or designated court). If origin is not an Apostille Convention state, obtain authentication from the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel exclusive alternatives and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent certificate of existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, tax authority, or other competent government agency in the country of incorporation of the foreign parent/promoter.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in origin -> if origin is an Apostille Convention state, obtain apostille from the designated Competent Authority. If origin is not an Apostille Convention state, obtain origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive routes and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and/or Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation, UBO disclosure, and registered office execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor or promoter.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution/PoA in the country of execution; if executed in an Apostille Convention state, apostille from the designated Competent Authority; if executed in a non-member state, authenticate through the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are parallel and exclusive, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (constitutive documents of foreign parent/promoter and draft Korean Chusik Hoesa Articles of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Promoter's law firm or corporate secretary; for the Korean entity's own draft articles, the Korean notary public and the promoter's legal counsel.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Foreign parent/promoter constitutive documents: notarization in origin, then apostille if origin is an Apostille Convention state or origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication plus Korean consular legalization if origin is not an Apostille Convention state. The Korean draft Articles of Association must separately be notarized by a Korean notary public before submission to the court registry. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign parent/promoter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the foreign parent/promoter's operational bank account.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank Reference Letter on bank letterhead, executed by an authorized bank officer and notarized or bank-certified; then, for use in Korea, obtain apostille from the relevant Competent Authority if the issuing bank is in an Apostille Convention state, or obtain origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by Korean consular legalization if the issuing bank is in a non-member state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory AML/KYC screening applies to each UBO, director, officer, and signatory at formation and on any change. Screening uses the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, the Republic of Korea's designated persons and warning lists, and PEP databases. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, documented source of wealth and source of funds, and senior management approval. For the low-risk bitumen wholesale business, standard CDD is maintained unless risk flags appear; all screening outputs are retained for at least five years under the Financial Transactions Report Act, and any hit or suspicious transaction is immediately escalated to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea, Internet Registration Office (IRO) - Commercial Company Name Clearance Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be in Hangul and must include the legal form indicator '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa). Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and symbols may be used in a parallel registered foreign name only as a supplement; Hangul remains the authoritative registry name. Phonetic transliteration of English words into Hangul follows the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism transliteration standard; the four-tier naming convention requires: (1) distinctive mark or token, (2) business descriptor, (3) selected entity suffix, and (4) registered foreign-language equivalent if desired. Names likely to be confused with a pre-existing registered business in the same business category are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires Financial Services Commission prior approval)
Securities (requires FSC and Korea Exchange approval)
National or Government (requires competent ministry authorization)
Hospital (requires Ministry of Health and Welfare authorization)
Patent, Attorney, or Accountant (reserved to licensed professionals)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, request a written rejection notice from the IRO or registry office. Within 14 calendar days of receipt, file an appeal petition with the competent District Court commercial registry, attaching the rejection notice, proposed Hangul trade name, name clause of the draft articles of incorporation, and an explanation of why the conflicting prior registered name or trademark has been abandoned. The registry director reviews the appeal on documentary evidence without a formal hearing. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a company-name action in the competent Administrative Court within 90 days, or immediately reserve a revised name. For sensitive-token refusals, the appeal must include the relevant ministerial approval documentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered office for a Korean Chusik Hoesa undertaking actual wholesale bitumen operations. The National Tax Service (NTS) and financial institutions require a real place of business for obtaining a business registration certificate, issuing electronic tax invoices, and opening a corporate bank account. A virtual office may only supplement a physical office where the company maintains desks, staff, records, and signage at that physical address. If management is offshore and no substantive Korean personnel exist, banks will decline account opening and the NTS may treat the entity as a paper corporation, disallow VAT input tax credits, and impose penalties. Full-service serviced offices are acceptable if they include a dedicated lease, reception, meeting room access, and independent mail handling.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 12 percent to 18 percent per year for a standard low-risk wholesale bitumen trader with a physical office, tax compliance, and active bank account; risk increases to 30 percent to 35 percent if the registered office is a mail forwarding address, a suspicious transaction report is filed, no employee is present during normal business hours, or annual turnover exceeds approximately KRW 2 billion. Inspection checklist: (1) lease contract under the corporation's name; (2) Korean-language signboard with the registered trade name; (3) workstations and reception with staff; (4) accounting books, invoices, and electronic tax invoice issuance system; (5) corporate bank statements; (6) utility bills; (7) business registration certificate; (8) minutes and records showing board decisions and commercial contracts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended through Act No. 18821 (2022), particularly Articles 288 (promoters), 289 (required contents of articles of incorporation), 292 (notarization of articles), 295 (subscription by promoters), 299 (examination), 312 (payment of shares and deposit certificate), 317 (registration of incorporation), 383 (number of directors), 390 (board of directors quorum and resolution), and 393 (board of directors authority); supplemented by the Framework Act on Foreign Investment, Articles 2 and 5, for non-resident shareholders, and the Corporate Registration Regulations under the Court Organization Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court (Seoul Central District Court Registry Office), Supreme Court Administration, Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act, filed together with the Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the Bank Deposit Certificate of Paid-in Capital
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa after the 2012 amendment to the Korean Commercial Act, and zero-won incorporation is legally available. However, Korean banking and trade finance practice, as well as the planned SWIFT LC and TT operations for imported containerized bitumen, require a fully deposited and verifiable paid-up capital. The promoters shall deposit at least KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 74,000) into a dedicated securities subscription escrow account (Jugeum Napseum Yesan) maintained with a licensed commercial bank. The escrowed funds must remain blocked until the court issues the Certificate of Incorporation Registration; any reimbursement to promoters before completion of registration constitutes a criminal offense under Article 628 of the Korean Commercial Act, and the bank-issued deposit certificate must be attached to the registration application as conclusive evidence of payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR CHUSIKHOESA (THE COMPANY), DULY CONVENED AND HELD ON THE DATE AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE IN SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, WITH THE QUORUM OF DIRECTORS AS REQUIRED UNDER ARTICLE 390 OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT, AND WITH THE PRESIDENCY OF THE CHAIRPERSON, WHO DECLARED THE MEETING LEGALLY CONSTITUTED.

SUBJECT 1 - VERIFICATION OF SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board examined the deposit certificate issued by the Bank pursuant to Article 312 of the Korean Commercial Act and verified that the sum of KRW 100,000,000, equal to the aggregate par value of 100,000 issued common shares at KRW 1,000 par value each, has been fully subscribed by the promoters and deposited into the restricted securities subscription account

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal (home.tax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for customs and export clearance data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean Chusik Hoesa must file a business registration application with the competent District Tax Office within 20 days from the commencement of business, submitting the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, lease/ownership evidence for the place of business, and the foreign passport/ID of representatives as applicable. The application is accepted through the HomeTax portal or at the District Tax Office, which issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number serving as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration ID. A foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business is registered by the NTS only where it has Korean VAT registration obligations (e.g., supply of electronic services or other taxable supplies to Korea) or a Korean permanent establishment; the foreign entity must submit certified copies of its foreign incorporation documents, articles/powers of attorney, and either a local place of business contract or appointment of a Korean tax representative. Registration is completed through HomeTax and the assigned business registration number must be used in all customs declarations, tax invoices, and VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxed at entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act; no check-the-box, pass-through, territorial, or hybrid mismatch elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - no economic turnover registration threshold; every business operator carrying on a business in Korea must be VAT-registered from the commencement of business. A simplified taxable person status exists for qualifying small traders but does not create a general registration threshold and is not relevant to wholesale bitumen trading.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A registered business operator must issue all VAT tax invoices electronically and transmit them to the NTS through the HomeTax e-tax invoice system or an NTS-approved Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) service provider no later than the day after issuance. There is no Latin-American style central digital stamp or real-time clearance; NTS operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice repository that continuously cross-checks invoice data against VAT returns and customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of containerized drummed/bagged penetration grade bitumen qualify for zero-rated VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are physically exported from Korea under a valid Korea Customs Service export declaration, the risk and title in the goods pass to the overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are received through a foreign exchange bank within the statutory repatriation deadline. Qualifying offshore digital services are not part of this physical goods mandate and are not relied upon for the bitumen wholesale scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration confirmation issued through the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system (Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (or Sea / Multimodal Transport Document) for the containerized bitumen showing the Korean seller as shipper and the foreign buyer as consignee/notify party
Foreign exchange bank certificate of export proceeds receipt or bank remittance advice evidencing receipt in freely convertible currency from the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and, where applicable, inspection certificate/cargo manifests matching the export declaration and Bill of Lading
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS will cross-check zero-rated export invoices against KCS UNI-PASS export declarations, Bills of Lading, and foreign exchange bank records. If the zero-rating is not fully substantiated, NTS retroactively assesses unpaid 10% VAT, imposes statutory additional taxes for unissued or false tax invoices (penalty of up to 3% of supply value for false e-tax invoices plus interest), and may refer the matter for criminal sanctions under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act if fraud or intentional false invoicing is identified. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day foreign exchange deadline can also trigger foreign exchange law penalties and removal of the zero-rate claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), operating in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN), as the primary monetary and financial stability authority. All cross-border foreign exchange transactions in the Republic of Korea are governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its attendant Enforcement Decree and Detailed Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions under the OECD code of liberalisation, meaning payments for goods, services, and ordinary profit remittances can be routed through authorized foreign exchange banks without central bank prior approval, subject to submission of underlying transaction documentation. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds, are regulated under a prior declaration or license system. Non-resident shareholders may freely remit dividends and disposal proceeds if they have satisfied the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act declaration requirements via a domestic bank. However, all export proceeds from the sale of bitumen and asphalt products must be collected through authorized domestic financial institutions and may be subject to prescribed surrender and collection timelines. Profit remittances by foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa entities require a tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service, confirming that corporate income tax, value-added tax, and withholding obligations have been discharged. There is no surrender requirement in the sense of forced conversion into KRW at a fixed rate; exporters may keep foreign currency proceeds in a designated foreign currency account, but they must be received within regulatory timeframes and reported to FEIN. Practical friction arises when the underlying purpose code is unclear or when capital contributions are made in-kind rather than in cash, as the bank will demand a verified valuation report and corporate registry amendment filing. Overall, KRW is convertible but operationally controlled, and a Chusik Hoesa engaged in bitumen wholesale must maintain meticulous documentary files to avoid freezing of trade payments, capital inflows, or dividend outflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 12 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Detailed Regulations on Foreign Exchange Transactions, export proceeds for goods shipped from the Republic of Korea must be collected within six months from the date of the export declaration or the date of shipment, whichever is applicable for the relevant trade method. Exporters may obtain an extension of up to two additional months from the authorized foreign exchange bank upon submission of a valid justification, such as documentary collection period delays or letters of credit negotiation timing. There is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring the export proceeds to be exchanged into KRW; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Account or convert at commercial bank rates. The entire invoice value must be received unless a justified discount, quality deduction, or open account offset has been properly reported with supporting trade documents and bank approval. Proceeds must be brought into Korea through an authorized Korean bank and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System within the applicable collection deadline; failure to collect or report triggers administrative fines and potential customs export blockages.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and Foreign Currency)
Trade Settlement Current Account with LC and Documentary Collection Services
Foreign Currency Receivables Account and Capital Injection Escrow Account
Operational Account for Commodity Trading and Supplier Payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, Airwallex, or Payoneer are effectively barred from serving as the primary transactional banking rail for a Korean Chusik Hoesa because they do not hold a Korean banking license and cannot provide KRW-denominated resident business settlement accounts or Korean Financial Services Commission authorizations for foreign exchange services. They may be used only peripherally for cross-border expense reimbursements or low-volume non-KRW treasury flows, but all substantive export collection, LC negotiation, tax payments, and capital verification must be conducted through an authorized Korean domestic bank. The legal viability rating for such EMIs is Low for this jurisdiction because the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires authorized foreign exchange bank handling, and virtual account issuance by unlicensed non-banks is prohibited. The treasury structure should therefore entirely depend on a tier-1 domestic commercial bank with a dedicated relationship manager for commodity wholesale trade.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory director or an authorized officer with corporate resolution and power-of-attorney is generally required to appear physically in-branch for initial account activation and execution of the account opening mandate in South Korea. The Financial Action Task Force-aligned Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) requires face-to-face verification of beneficial owners and directors for non-resident corporate clients, with biometric ID scanning, original corporate registration documents, and a wet-ink signature or digital signature certificate. Remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly permitted by all tier-1 banks; some banks allow a Korean-appointed legal representative or local accountant to attend in person, but the financial institution retains discretion to demand the statutory director appear for an in-person interview if the KYC risk score is elevated. For a bitumen wholesale entity with a lower AML risk tier, the practical path is to have the foreign director physically travel to Seoul or Busan once, accompanied by apostilled certificates and a local tax representative, to satisfy the bank's 'know your customer' mandate and obtain clearing rails for trade transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership concentration with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain involving intermediates registered in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full ownership cascade chart ending in the physical individual shareholders; certified extracts from the Korean Corporate Registry confirming the Chusik Hoesa's shareholder ledger; apostilled certificates of incorporation and registered agent certificates for each intermediate holding vehicle; sworn affidavits from all beneficial owners; proof of source of funds such as audited financial statements of the parent entity or personal tax returns and bank statements covering the last 12 months for each beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag arising from invoice values inconsistent with industry benchmarks for drummed and bagged bitumen
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent third-party commodity valuation certificates issued by an accredited surveyor (e.g., SGS, Cotecna or Intertek) for the specific shipment; original bills of lading, container numbers, seal numbers, and port of loading terminal receipts; vessel charter party or freight invoice demonstrating realistic Incoterms; customs declaration forms (Korea Customs Service import/export declarations); supplier purchase contracts and agent commission agreements; and a bank-provided historical transaction profile showing normal billing prices for ISIC 4661 wholesale trades.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose code mismatch between declared trade in bitumen and suspected involvement in asphalt paving services or government infrastructure contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legally reviewed wholesale supply agreement explicitly excluding installation, paving, and construction services; end-user certificates from overseas buyers declaring purchase solely for onward commodity wholesale; the entity's corporate register business purpose statement limited to wholesale supply under ISIC 4661 and NAICS 424720; technical specification sheets for the grade of bitumen; and a clean tax compliance certificate from the National Tax Service confirming no VAT misclassification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual volume of high-value or phased transactions with targeted countries, failing to match the low-risk commercial model of a bitumen wholesaler
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive trade flow calendar with each shipment's LC number, MT103 SWIFT reference, invoice, and customs entry number; the bank's official risk questionnaire completed by the compliance officer; proof that all payments will follow the established 'letter of credit only' payment method for jurisdictions with elevated sanctions risks; corporate minutes approving risk thresholds; and a signed undertaking to immediately report any deviation from the declared commodity and payment profile to the Korea Customs Service and KoFIU.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into a Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed through an authorized domestic foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 or MT202. The remitter must reference the Foreign Exchange Declaration code under the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System, typically code 380101 for 'Foreign direct investment in a newly incorporated domestic company'. The remitter must ensure the capital contribution is in the same currency as stated in the foreign direct investment notification filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or the designated bank. The bank will issue a Certificate of Foreign Direct Investment Registration (외국인투자기업 등록증 유사 기능 in substance) but in English, the 'Certificate of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration' after verification of the inward remittance and the corporate registry amendment. Capital verification requires the registered capital to be fully deposited in a temporary capital escrow account; funds cannot be used for operating expenses until the court-affiliated registry has updated the company's paid-in capital and the certified capital verification report has been issued by the appointed external auditor or a certified public accountant. The injector's identity must match the corporate registry shareholder records; any third-party wire is prohibited unless accompanied by a notarized subrogation agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for bitumen procurement, freight payment, and supplier settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 transfers, irrevocable letters of credit (LC at sight or usance) opened by the Korean bank in favour of overseas suppliers, or documentary collections (D/P and D/A) where the transaction size is moderate and trust is established. Every outbound payment must include the appropriate Foreign Exchange purpose code, such as 310101 for general trade payments under import of goods, and must be supported by the underlying import contract, proforma invoice, and bill of lading. The clearing rail for LC operations is SWIFT MT700/MT701, with reimbursement occurring through SWIFT MT740/MT750; the merchant bank must effect payment through SWIFT MT202 COV. For containerized bitumen shipments, the bank will also require ISPM 15 wood package compliance certificates and the customs export declaration in the buyer's jurisdiction to ensure the LC documents are compliant. Korean banks typically settle KRW transactions through the Bank of Korea's electronic settlement system (BOK-Wire) and foreign currency transactions through the respective currency clearing system (CHIPS, TARGET2, or CIPS for CNY). Only onshore licensed foreign exchange banks may provide these rails, and all outbound trades are monitored by KoFIU for trade-based money laundering typologies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (plain vanilla KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, KRW/CNY) with an underlying real trade exposure, permitted for the bitumen wholesale entity for hedging forecasted export or import cash flows within 12 months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW conducted offshore with global banks for hedging currency exposure when the entity does not hold sufficient onshore export contracts to justify a physical deliverable forward.

Onshore participation in liquid mainstream currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps for balance sheet hedging of foreign-currency borrowings, provided the swap transaction is specifically approved by the bank's treasury products desk and the maturity does not exceed the underlying debt duration.

Buying or selling of foreign exchange options with premium payment in KRW, restricted to hedging known commitments, and only when the notional amount does not exceed 2 times the actual underlying trade flow to remain compliant with Korean 'real demand' principles.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and retention of annual financial statements at the regular general shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General shareholders' meeting of the Chusik Hoesa; approved statements and meeting minutes are retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies must hold the meeting by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular shareholders' meeting exposes responsible directors to administrative fines under Commercial Act Article 635; no administrative strike-off applies in the Korean registry system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with attached financial statements and local corporate income surtax schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through HomeTax and the competent local tax office for the local corporate income surtax portion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies file by March 31, with extension to May 31 when statutory external audit applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or erroneous filing triggers unfaithful-payment penalty tax up to 20% or fraud penalty tax up to 40% plus statutory overdue interest and enforced collection; no administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested company status report including foreign equity percentage and ultimate beneficial owner confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the competent customs office as designated under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies must file by January 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or submission of false information triggers an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may restrict foreign-investment benefits; no administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory auditor's report when the compulsory external audit threshold is exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General shareholders' meeting; auditor report accompanies the tax return to the National Tax Service and is filed with the relevant financial supervisory reporting portal where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Report must be presented in time for the annual general shareholders' meeting; audit procedures and deadlines are governed by the Act on External Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors of a company subject to external audit who fail to obtain an audit may be subject to corrective orders, criminal penalties, and loss of the extended corporate tax return filing deadline; no administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal verification of corporate registers and registration of any shareholding or officer changes with the district court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District court commercial registry having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; Korea does not require an annual registry renewal filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register changes must be filed promptly after each event; internal register verification is recommended before the March 31 shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered changes may not be asserted against third parties and responsible officers may incur administrative fines under the Commercial Registration Act; no administrative strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit applies to a non-listed Chusik Hoesa when total assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year are equal to or greater than KRW 12 billion. Listed companies, financial institutions, companies designated as public-interest entities, and companies otherwise subject to group disclosure under Korean external audit regulations are audited regardless of asset size. Small and medium-sized entity exemptions or adjustments may apply as prescribed by the Presidential Decree under the Act on External Audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed companies and designated entities; non-listed private companies may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) unless K-IFRS is otherwise required under the Act on External Audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Chusik Hoesa must maintain accurate share register records and must report foreign-invested company status, foreign equity percentages, and changes in foreign ownership to KOTRA or a designated authority within 15 days after fiscal year-end. Korea does not operate a separate central UBO annual filing with the Companies Registry; beneficial owner confirmation is event-driven and is also submitted to domestic financial institutions under FATCA/CRS and Korea Anti-Money-Laundering customer due diligence requirements. Share transfers are legally effective against the company only when the transferee is entered in the register of members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditors or Audit Committee Members
Minutes of Board of Directors' Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top statutory rate; progressive brackets of 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% above KRW 20 billion; a 10% local income tax surcharge is added, producing a combined maximum statutory rate of 23.1%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory corporate income tax holiday applies to wholesale bitumen or asphalt trading. Standard tax preferences include tax credits for qualifying R&D expenditure, facility investment, job creation, and foreign-invested high-tech manufacturing in Free Economic Zones (up to 100% income tax exemption for 5 years and 50% for 2 years). A passive wholesale logistics entity does not ordinarily qualify for such zone-based reductions.
